simple.meaning: יָקַץ (yâqats) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to awake (intransitive).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 10 times in Genesis, Judges, 1 Kings, Psalms, beginning at Genesis 9:24. The surrounding contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָקַץ (H3364) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יָקַץ (yâqats) / H3364 is traced through Genesis 9:24, Genesis 28:16, Genesis 41:4, Genesis 41:7 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3364. yaqats [ יָקַץ ] verb awake (Arabic wake, be awake ) — Qal Imperfect יִקָ֑ץ 1Kin 18:27 ; וַיִּיקַץ Gen 28:16 3 t.; וַיִּקַץ Judg 16:20 ; Psa 78:65 ; 1Kin 3:15 (see Baer); וָאִיקָ֑ץ Gen 41:21 ; יִָֽקְצוּ Hab 2:7 ; — awake , Gen 41:4 , 7 , 21 (E), 1Kin 3:15 ; of Baal 18:27 ; followed by מִשְּׁנָתוֺ Gen 28:16 (J), Judg 16:14 , 20 ; of Noah, מִיֵּינוֺ Gen 9:24 (J), i.e. from drunken sleep; figurative of ׳י Psa 78:65 , i.e. become suddenly active ; of enemies Hab 2:7 . — See also קיץ Hiph`il

occurrences.englishText: Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his youngest son had done to him.
Jacob awakened out of his sleep, and he said, “Surely Yahweh is in this place, and I didn’t know it.”
The ugly and thin cattle ate up the seven sleek and fat cattle. So Pharaoh awoke.
The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven healthy and full ears. Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.
and when they had eaten them up, it couldn’t be known that they had eaten them, but they were still ugly, as at the beginning. So I awoke.
She fastened it with the pin, and said to him, “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” He awakened out of his sleep, and plucked away the pin of the beam and the fabric.
She said, “The Philistines are upon you, Samson!”

Solomon awoke; and behold, it was a dream. Then he came to Jerusalem, and stood before the ark of Yahweh’s covenant, and offered up burnt offerings, offered peace offerings, and made a feast for all his servants.
At noon, Elijah mocked them, and said, “Cry aloud; for he is a god. Either he is deep in thought, or he has gone somewhere, or he is on a journey, or perhaps he sleeps and must be awakened.”
